newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA OPPOSITION WALKS OUT OF PARLT AMID PROTESTS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA OPPOSITION WALKS OUT OF PARLT AMID PROTESTS.

text.p: Thousands protested outside Bulgaria's parliament on Friday as the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) walked out, when the ruling Socialists, rejected a vote on a "salvation declaration" proposed by the UDF.

The opposition proposed the "salvation declaration" last month calling for elections to be held in March, and negotiations with the IMF and World Bank on an economic programme to be conducted by an all-party team.
The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), which holds a majority in parliament, proposed to insert in the declaration parts of socialist declaration submitted on Thursday.
"Replacing texts in our delaration is cynical," UDF deputy and ex-prime minister Filip Dimitrov told parliament announcing the walk out.
UDF leader Ivan Kostov they will decide on further actions in meeting during the weekend.
The opposition staged every-day chain nation-wide protests since last week pressing for the approval of the declaration.
"The BSP, which led the country to its gravest crisis in history, has no right to rule," said head of the UDF parliamentary group Yordan Sokolov.
A human chain of mostly students surrounded parliament, which was heavily gaurded by riot police.

Thousands of protesters burning red flags marched to the parliament building demanding early elections. They chanted "Elections" and carried signs saying "Red rubbish, out" and "The prime minister is a policeman, the country is a labour camp".

On Wednesday the Socialists nominated powerful Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev to become prime minister in place of outgoing Zhan Videnov, who resigned on December 21 after severe criticism of his management of the economy.
Hundreds of taxis cruised central streets in Sofia with lit headlights and sounded horns.
"One party delared war on its people and put its people behind the wire of isolation," a trade union activist told the rally.
Opposition deputies joined the protesters outside parliaments saying that they will step up protests next week.
Protesters hurled snow balls at socialist deputies walking out of the parliament building.

The opposition says the BSP, formed by leading Communists after the collapse of one-party rule in 1989, has failed to tackle the country's economic crisis and no longer has enough support to form a government.
